solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Where numbers are called, not to share writer’s point about everything (5,4)

indicatorNotes.about: turns HOG and NIB around, so they read back to front

blocks.note: to hog something is to keep it all and not share

annotation.surface: Someone refuses to share while making a writer's point about everything, in a place where numbers get read out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'about' covers only HOG and NIB, not ALL, which is simply added on the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: bingo is the game where a caller reads out numbers, and the hall is the place it happens.

entries.clue: Rock singer’s dicky but not having temperature (5)

indicatorNotes.but not having: tells you to take a letter away from the dicky

blocks.note: a dicky bow is a bow tie

annotation.surface: A rock singer is feeling poorly, though without a fever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'dicky' in the surface means unwell; here it is a bow tie, from the British 'dicky bow'. The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: David Bowie is one rock singer among many.

entries.clue: Innocence of crackers eaten around four (7)

indicatorNotes.crackers: crazy, so the letters of EATEN are scrambled
indicatorNotes.around: the scrambled letters wrap themselves around IV

blocks.note: four in Roman numerals, placed inside

annotation.surface: A childlike innocence about crackers being eaten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits in the surface; here it means mad and scrambles EATEN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: naivety is innocence of the world's ways.

entries.clue: Film’s original poster writer, the guy one’s flipping about (11)

indicatorNotes.flipping: to flip something is to turn it over, so RE comes out back to front

blocks.note: internet forum shorthand for whoever started a thread

annotation.surface: A film's first poster shows a writer and some fellow turning over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film's original poster' reads as one phrase; it splits after 'Film'. OP for the person who opened an online thread is modern slang.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the 2023 Christopher Nolan biopic of the atom-bomb physicist is one film.

entries.clue: Some stars in Cannes, at The City on the Baltic (6)

blocks.note: capital of Latvia, a Baltic port

annotation.surface: Film stars at Cannes, and a city on the Baltic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some stars in Cannes' pulls towards film stars at the festival; the definition is just 'Some stars', a constellation. The capital T of 'The' is only there for the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A constellation is a named group of stars, and Auriga, the Charioteer, is one of them.

entries.clue: Babe almost breaking into silly expression (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: drop the last letter of CUTIE
indicatorNotes.breaking into: something that breaks into a place ends up inside it, so CUTI goes inside LOON

blocks.note: a loon is a silly person; the outer part
CUTIE (a babe) without its last letter

annotation.surface: An infant nearly bursts into a daft phrase.
annotation.walkthrough: 'silly' stands for a noun here, a loon.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a locution is a word or phrase, a particular way of putting things.

entries.clue: A problem / affected one (5)

blocks.note: someone who strikes attitudes and puts on airs

annotation.walkthrough: A puzzle that poses a question and a show-off who poses for effect share the same word.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses come from 'pose': to set a question and to strike an attitude.

entries.clue: This character would advance by 18 places if hosted by Musk, say (3)

annotation.definition: This character would advance by 18 places if hosted by Musk, say

blocks.clueFragment: This character would advance by 18 places
blocks.note: a letter of an alphabet, moving 18 places along it
Elon Musk: put the letter's name inside ELON

annotation.surface: A letter would jump 18 spots up a ranking if Elon Musk took it on.
annotation.walkthrough: Put PSI inside ELON and you get E-PSI-LON, EPSILON. Psi is the 23rd Greek letter and epsilon the 5th, 18 places apart. You need the answer to check it, so solve from the crossers.
annotation.definitionFit: Psi is a Greek letter, and the arithmetic of the Greek alphabet is the whole clue.

entries.clue: Parental dude initially in another’s place? (7)

annotation.definition: Parental dude initially in another’s place?

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of Parental and dude

blocks.note: in another's stead = in their place; the outer part
first letters of Parental and dude

annotation.surface: A fatherly figure stepping into someone else's role.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: a stepdad is a parental dude who has taken the place of another.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes a stepfather: a fatherly man filling a role that was once someone else's.

entries.clue: What’s made early, to be nuked? (5,4)

annotation.definition: What’s made early, to be nuked?

indicatorNotes.to be nuked: something nuked is blasted apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

annotation.surface: Something prepared in advance for destruction by nuclear weapons.
annotation.walkthrough: 'nuked' is also slang for microwaved, so the whole clue describes the answer: a dinner made in advance, waiting for the microwave.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes a supermarket meal cooked in advance and reheated in a microwave.

entries.clue: Passing idea for a moan (7)

blocks.note: a whim is a passing fancy
per = for a, as in 'ten pounds per head'

annotation.surface: A fleeting thought about complaining.
annotation.walkthrough: 'for a' looks like a link joining idea to moan; it is the wordplay, PER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a whimper is a feeble, low moaning cry.

entries.clue: Unrealistic dream of such as Big Ben area (7)

blocks.note: Big Ben is a bell that chimes

annotation.surface: A fanciful dream about the area round Big Ben.
annotation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the great bell in the clock tower at Westminster, so it is a chimer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Chimera was a fire-breathing monster of Greek myth, so the word came to mean any wild, impossible fancy.

entries.clue: A kind of dam incorporated by Sizewell (3)

blocks.note: the answer is in the middle of this word

annotation.surface: A kind of dam built into the Sizewell power station.
annotation.walkthrough: Sizewell is a nuclear power station on the Suffolk coast, so 'dam' suggests water engineering; it is a mother animal, as in a horse's sire and dam.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a dam is an animal's mother, and a ewe is a mother sheep.

entries.clue: Contrasts in light / musical number (5,3,3)

blocks.note: the dark and light halves of the clock

annotation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song, not a figure: the Cole Porter standard 'Night and Day'.
annotation.definitionFit: Night and day are the two opposites of light, and 'Night and Day' is a Cole Porter song.

entries.clue: Dogger’s crude? (5,3,3)

blocks.note: not a dog walker but the sea area Dogger

annotation.surface: A dog walker's rude remark.
annotation.walkthrough: Dogger is a sea area in the North Sea, named in the British shipping forecast; 'crude' is crude oil, not rudeness.
annotation.definitionFit: Oil drilled from under the North Sea, where Dogger lies, is North Sea crude.

entries.clue: Kitchen rod that’s twisted more? (6)

blocks.note: a comparative: more skew, more askew

annotation.surface: A kitchen rod that has been bent even further.
annotation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a made-up comparative, SKEW-ER, flagged by the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A skewer is a kitchen rod, and read as skew plus -er it means more twisted.

entries.clue: City mob is somehow producing mutual advantage (9)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters are put together in some other way

annotation.surface: A city's gangsters are somehow creating a win-win arrangement.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is the first three words, all nine letters used once.
annotation.definitionFit: In biology a symbiotic relationship is one that benefits both partners.

entries.clue: Bird, type of pheasant that’s alternatively used for art (8)

indicatorNotes.used for: OR takes the place of ART

blocks.note: a game bird related to the pheasant
ART in PARTRIDGE is swapped for OR

annotation.surface: A game bird whose image is used in art.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bird' looks like the partridge; it is the definition, British slang for a prison sentence, as is porridge (also the TV sitcom).
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: both bird and porridge mean time served in prison.

entries.clue: Bad man with bad deed cut short American’s ride (8)

indicatorNotes.cut short: drop the last letter of ACT

blocks.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
ill = bad, as in ill will

annotation.surface: A villain whose wicked act was curtailed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'ride' is slang for a car, and the Cadillac is a classic American make.

entries.clue: Greek character actor without subtlety, crazy man (8)

annotation.surface: A Greek character actor lacking finesse, a lunatic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character actor' reads as one role; split after 'character'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Muhammad is a man's name, among the most common in the world.

entries.clue: Where might bowler rest? Hard answer to follow (7)

annotation.surface: A cricketer asks where a bowler might take a breather.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball; here the bowler is a round hat.
annotation.definitionFit: A bowler is a round felt hat, and a rack for hats is where one is hung up.

entries.clue: Part — or place? — of union (6)

blocks.note: a branch of a trade union in printing or newspapers
a place of worship, where a wedding joins a couple

annotation.surface: A question about which section of a trade union is meant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'of union' belongs to both definitions: part of a trade union, and a place of union where couples marry.
annotation.definitionFit: A chapel is a printers' union branch and a place where marriages are made.

entries.clue: Soft food and drink lifted with a mild spice (7)

indicatorNotes.lifted: in a down clue, KIR is raised so it reads upwards

blocks.note: the clue's a, kept as is

annotation.surface: Baby food and a drink raised, seasoned with a gentle spice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'lifted' only makes sense as a reversal in a down clue, where the letters read from the bottom up.
annotation.definitionFit: Paprika, ground from sweet red peppers, is the gentle cousin of cayenne.

entries.clue: Part of parliamentary address, according to someone whipping (6)

blocks.note: SW1, the Westminster postcode, with 1 as I

annotation.surface: A whip's view of part of a parliamentary speech.
annotation.walkthrough: 'address' suggests a speech; it is a postal address, SW1 being the London postcode of Parliament. Whipping is slang for stealing, so a swiper is a thief.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British: to whip and to swipe both mean to steal.

entries.clue: Bury rival with diminutive person answering questions (11)

annotation.surface: Burying a competitor alongside a small questioned person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bury' is also a Lancashire town, and 'diminutive person' tempts you to read one phrase; 'diminutive' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the one being interviewed is the one answering.

entries.clue: Half of metal for a mug’s seat (3)

indicatorNotes.Half of: keep the first three of six letters

blocks.note: tankards are often made of this tin alloy
keep the first three of the six letters

annotation.surface: A mug's seat, made half of metal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'a mug's seat' seems to go together; the 's is 'is', and the definition is only 'seat'.
annotation.definitionFit: A pew is a bench seat in church; 'take a pew' means sit down.

entries.clue: They say my life is easy, with a grimace? (5)

indicatorNotes.They say: what follows is heard, not seen

blocks.note: an easy life is 'the life of Riley'

annotation.surface: A smug claim to an easy life, made with a twisted smile.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The life of Riley' is an idiom for a carefree life; RILEY is said like WRYLY. The question mark admits that wryly means with a twisted face only loosely.
annotation.definitionFit: Wry first meant twisted, so a wry face is a grimace, and doing something wryly is doing it with one.

entries.clue: To catch public transport, first brace for Metropolitan Line (7)

indicatorNotes.first brace: a brace is a pair, so take the first two letters

blocks.note: the first pair of letters of Metropolitan

annotation.surface: Rushing to board a tram, then the Metropolitan line of the London Underground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Metropolitan Line' is a London Underground line, but the words split: 'Line' gives only L. A brace is a pair, as of pheasants.
annotation.definitionFit: A trammel is a fishing net, and to trammel is to entangle or catch.

entries.clue: Former prime minister / is allowed / 31 days (3)

annotation.walkthrough: A triple definition: Theresa May, 'you may' for permission, and the month of May, which has 31 days.
annotation.definitionFit: Theresa May was prime minister, 'may' means is allowed, and May is a 31-day month.

entries.clue: Dig round memorial in upright state (7)

indicatorNotes.round: one word goes round the other like a ring, so PRY encloses OBIT

blocks.note: to pry is to dig into, poke about

annotation.surface: Digging round a memorial in a standing position.
annotation.walkthrough: 'upright' sounds physical; it means honest.
annotation.definitionFit: Upright here is moral, not physical: probity is the quality of being honest and decent.

entries.clue: A minor possibly trailing about like a sponge? (5)

indicatorNotes.trailing: to trail is to follow behind, so the key comes after CA

blocks.note: A minor is one example of a musical key

annotation.surface: A child dragging about looking soggy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A minor' looks like a child; it is the musical key. The definition's question mark says a sponge here is a cake.
annotation.definitionFit: A sponge is a kind of cake, so something like a sponge is cakey.

entries.clue: Consequence of run in yard, rounding run out (9)

indicatorNotes.rounding: to round something is to go all the way about it, so COLLAR circles RO

blocks.note: to run in and to collar both mean to arrest

annotation.surface: A result of a run in the yard that ended in a run-out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'run in yard' pulls towards exercise; 'run in' is British slang for arrest, so COLLAR. RO is how a scorecard records a batsman run out.
annotation.definitionFit: From logic: a corollary is a result that follows from one already proved, so a consequence.
